title: Consolidate tokenizer handshake and deterministic template mapping for onboarding
creator: Asha Patel
body:
Summary:
We are seeing intermittent failures during model onboarding where the tokenizer metadata emitted by model importers doesn't align deterministically with chat template expectations. This causes subtle role delimiter mismatches and malformed prefix/suffix tokens that break runtime framing and lead to degraded latency for some models and failed profile publishing.

Goal:
Create a deterministic 'tokenizer handshake' and mapping layer that:
- fingerprints tokenizer metadata and chat templates (template fingerprinting)
- applies a deterministic mapping/normalization (role-affix normalization) to reconcile differences
- gates profile publish when compatibility guarantees cannot be met and provides a clear remediation path for model owners
- surfaces telemetry and actionable alerts in Console before onboarding finalization

Acceptance criteria:
- Tokenizer handshake library (python + go wrappers) that can produce a compatibility report artifact during onboarding: checksum, token boundary heuristics, mapped-template preview, confidence score.
- Onboarding pipeline integrated preflight check that will:
  - automatically attempt deterministic mappings for common mismatches (whitespace, subtoken-splitting of role markers, invisible control chars)
  - mark onboarding as 'blocked - mapping required' with human-friendly remediation if mapping fails above confidence threshold
- Performance profile publishing will be suppressed for blocked models; when mapping completes, publishing resumes and profile is annotated with mapping details and tokenizer checksum.
- Telemetry emitted: counts of blocked onboards, mapping success rate, runtime fallback activations, and end-to-end tokenization mismatch rate. Dashboards in Console should show these within 24 hours of rollout.
- Tests: unit fuzzing (1000 random templates per supported tokenizer), integration tests in onboarding CI, and a blue/green canary rollout to 10% of new onboarding jobs for 48 hours.

Background / Context:
Recently, multiple onboarding incidents traced to edge-case tokenization behavior (see incident notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/incidents/2025-02-tokenizer-fragmentation) and two PRs that attempted ad-hoc fixes (PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6120, https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboard-scripts/pull/141). The current importer relies on best-effort heuristics that are non-deterministic across language bindings and model packaging. That unpredictability caused profile mismatches (published profiles that don't reflect runtime framing), leading to customer confusion and occasional runtime errors.

Design decisions / trade-offs:
- Deterministic mapping vs permissive runtime fallback: we opt for deterministic preflight mapping to prevent publishing inaccurate profiles. Runtime fallbacks remain available but will be annotated and rate-limited.
- Fingerprint algorithm: use SHA256 of normalized tokenizer metadata + template AST + canonical whitespace normalization. This is conservative but easy to audit.
- Confidence scoring: rule-based heuristics (token-boundary alignment, token-count delta, role-marker preservation). We will avoid opaque ML models for now to keep debugging fast.

Implementation plan:
1) Library: implement tokenizer-handshake in Python (lib/token_handshake.py) with a Go shim used by the onboarding microservice. Provide a CLI that outputs a JSON compatibility artifact (note: artifact is for human consumption and must be stored in onboarding artifacts bucket).
2) Onboarding pipeline changes: call handshake CLI as a preflight step. If mapping required and auto-map confidence >= 0.85, apply mapping and proceed. Otherwise create a remediation ticket & block publish.
3) Profile publishing: modify publisher to check for compatibility artifact; if absent or blocked, mark profile as DRAFT and do not publish to catalog. When mapping completes, attach mapping metadata and publish.
4) Console + Telemetry: emit events to metrics pipeline (blocked_onboards_total, mapping_auto_applied_total, mapping_failure_total, profile_publish_blocked_total). Add initial dashboard tiles and alert with runbook.
5) Tests & Fuzzing: add unit tests covering normalized examples from incident store and run fuzzing harness in CI (1000 templates per tokenizer implementation).
6) Rollout: Canary at 10% of onboarding jobs for 48 hours, then 50% for 72 hours, then full rollout. Backout plan documented if blocked_onboards spikes > 5% baseline or any critical customer onboarding fails.

Implementation notes / PRs:
- Proposed PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboard-scripts/pull/198 (handshake lib), https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6253 (publisher gating), https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/409 (dashboard tiles)
- Artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Tokenizer+Handshake+Design; fuzz corpus: gs://redwood-onboard/fuzz/tokenizer-corpus-2025-02.tar.gz

Open questions / blockers:
- Language binding parity: go shim must be reviewed to ensure deterministic behavior between Python and Go runtimes (security review not required but important).
- Do we want to allow model owners to opt into permissive publishing for speed? (product decision)

Progress updates / Timeline log:
- 2025-02-28: Ticket created (Asha). Scoped goals and acceptance criteria.
- 2025-03-01: Prototype handshake CLI that computes checksum and simple token boundary diff (Miguel). See prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboard-scripts/pull/198
- 2025-03-03: Integration spike ran with 200 onboarding artifacts; auto-mapping success rate ~88%, edge-case failures flagged for manual remediation. Telemetry hooks drafted (Sergio reviewed).
- 2025-03-05: Design review with Runtime and Console teams. Agreed on fingerprint format and confidence threshold (0.85). Follow-up: add fuzz harness to CI and provide mapping preview to model owner UI.
- 2025-03-07: Started work on runtime publisher gating. Draft PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6253 (WIP).

Review feedback / action items:
- PM (Leah O'Connor): add product-facing copy for remediation flow and allow a one-click override post-approval. (action: include override audit log)
- Security (Rajiv Menon): confirm CLI artifact storage perms and ensure no secrets are embedded in artifacts. (action: add artifact storage ACL check)
- Design (Priya Shah): create mapping preview UI mockups for Console. (action: design handoff to frontend)

Rollout & Monitoring:
- Canary metric guardrails: mapping_auto_applied_total / onboarding_total should remain >= 0.6 during canary, mapping_failure_total must not increase > 2x baseline. Any critical regression triggers rollback.
- Post-rollout tasks: run 7-day report comparing published profiles vs runtime framing for new models and publish learnings to Confluence.

Follow-ups after Done:
- Automate suggestions to model owners based on common failure clusters (e.g., normalize invisible role markers).
- Consider light ML-based mapping if rule-based heuristics plateau.

Links & references:
- Incident note: https://confluence.redwood.ai/incidents/2025-02-tokenizer-fragmentation
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Tokenizer+Handshake+Design
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboard-scripts/pull/198
- Runtime gating PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6253
- Profile publishing changes (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/publisher/pull/77

Owner notes:
- Keep mapping_auto_applied as auditable change. Ensure one-click override requires approval and is logged against user identity.
- Coordinate with Solutions Eng for any high-touch customer onboarding during rollout windows.
